## LLM-ASSISTANT (decomposed 2026-08-02) — in-match local-LLM command assistant · **WAVE 0 ONLY** (TASK-409..426); Waves 1–2 are gated one-liners

**The feature in one line:** the player types a natural-language order — *"send 10 footmen with a sorcerer to the nearest ancient ground"* — and a **local LLM shipped inside the game** translates it into the game's existing unit commands, surveying state first and asking a clarifying question when the request cannot be met.

**Design authority = Jonathan's approved plan `C:\Users\wesel\.claude\plans\there-is-one-new-glittery-bentley.md`** — it carries the research findings, the architecture, the six spike bars and the Wave 0/1/2 breakdown. **The plan file wins over any board summary.** Read it before starting any task in this batch; these specs do not re-derive it.

**Jonathan's four rulings (DECIDED — no assignee re-opens them):** (i) **CPU fallback required** — must run on the modal 8 GB Steam card AND CPU-only, no vendor lock-in (⇒ **Vulkan + CPU backend, never CUDA**); (ii) **V1 = text-only vertical slice** — in-match console, the order verbs + unit selection, the clarification loop; **no voice, no macro UI, no settings screen**; (iii) **command only** — the AI never plays cards and never spends gold; (iv) **prompt-engineer first**, fine-tune only if measurement demands it.

**LAW WAS WRITTEN FIRST (house rule):** CONVENTIONS **"In-match LLM command assistant (v1, text-only) — 2026-08-02"** — 10 sub-sections: the central law · the strictly-additive law · symbols-only · the unit-registry rejection · naming/folder law · **the two manager rulings** · licensing + repo hygiene · prompt layout/threading/multiplayer posture · **the pinned cross-task signature registry** · tunables.

### ⚠️ WAVE 0 OPENS WITH A GO/NO-GO SPIKE. THIS IS BOARDED AS A SPIKE, NOT AS A FIRST INSTALMENT.

**TASK-409 → 410/411 → 412 → 413 exists to answer whether this feature ships at all.** Its six measurements can kill it. The bars, from the plan:

| # | Measure | Bar |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Frame-time delta during prefill/decode — hitch histogram, **worst + p99, never mean** — across full-offload / partial / CPU-only | **No frame > 33 ms** attributable to inference on the **partial** tier |
| 2 | TTFT + wall-clock for ~60 constrained tokens, warm prefix | **≤ 2 s partial · ≤ 6 s CPU-only** |
| 3 | KV-prefix reuse works — prefill tokens turn 1 vs turn 2 | **~70 % drop.** If not, the prompt layout is wrong and must be fixed *first* |
| 4 | Peak VRAM + RSS with the game at *its* peak | Fits 8 GB with room |
| 5 | Accuracy on **40 hand-written Siegebound sentences** (ours, not BFCL) — exact match on `{intent, kinds, counts, where}` | **≥ 85 %.** Below: better few-shots → tighter grammar → bigger model → *only then* fine-tune |
| 6 | Does a focused `UEditableTextBox` starve Enhanced Input of WASD? | Binary; determines the console's input fallback |

**⛔ NOTHING IN WAVE 1 IS WRITTEN UNTIL THE SPIKE REPORTS.** That is a hard gate, restated on every Wave 1 one-liner.
**⚠️ RUN IT IN PIE ON `L_Arena` WITH UNITS ON THE FIELD — never an empty map.** The entire risk being measured is *contention*; an empty-map number is worse than no number because it looks like evidence.

### ⛔ BUILD-GATE SERIALIZATION — READ BEFORE DISPATCHING ANYTHING IN THIS BATCH (added 2026-08-02, after a live defect)

**TASK-401 (the FOLLOW lane's compile gate) FAILED on three diagnostics from THIS batch's `SiegeAssistantCommand.cpp` and `SiegeAssistantSnapshot.cpp`** — files a live agent was actively writing while that build ran. **The FOLLOW lane itself compiled completely clean.** A clean lane was failed by a lane it has nothing to do with. Law: CONVENTIONS **"⛔ THE QUIET-MODULE LAW — build-gate serialization (2026-08-02)"**.

> **FILE-DISJOINTNESS IS NOT BUILD-DISJOINTNESS.** `Source/GitClaudeUnrealTest/` is ONE UBT module; any in-flight `.cpp` in it — **even a brand-new file owned by an unrelated batch** — is compiled by, and can fail, every other lane's compile gate. **A compile gate requires a QUIET MODULE, not merely non-overlapping files.**

Concretely, for this batch:
1. **TASK-416 · 417 · 418 · 411 are game-module programmer tasks. NONE may be in flight while ANY compile gate runs** — including **TASK-401** (FOLLOW) and **TASK-420 / TASK-422 / TASK-425** (this batch). Their `▶ NOW` marking means "no task blocker", **not** "safe beside a build".
2. **TASK-420 and TASK-401 are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE.** So are TASK-420 / TASK-422 / TASK-425 with each other and with TASK-403.
3. **✅ TASK-409 · 410 · 423 · 426 ARE GENUINELY PARALLEL-SAFE AGAINST A GAME-MODULE GATE** — 409/410/423 live in `Plugins/SiegeLlama/`, **a SEPARATE UBT module**, and 426 is a `Docs/Data/` CSV that compiles nothing. ⚠️ **This is a concrete, now-demonstrated payoff of ruling B's plugin split — when a game-module gate is imminent, prefer plugin-side work.**
4. **DIAGNOSTIC ATTRIBUTION:** a failure is attributed to **the file the diagnostic names**, never to the lane that ran the build. Foreign diagnostics route to the owning batch's QA gate as **early information** and are **never** recorded as the running lane's findings or counted against its QA loop budget.
5. **A CONTAMINATED GATE IS RE-RUN, NOT RE-LITIGATED.** Never "fix" another batch's in-flight file to make your own gate pass — that is a single-owner violation stacked on a serialization violation.

### Manager rulings (binding for TASK-409..425)

1. **🔨 RULING A — THE CONSOLE WIDGET'S TREE IS CODE-AUTHORED IN V1.** Explicit deviation from the `U<Name>Widget` ↔ `WBP_<Name>` law, granted as a **named, scoped, conditional exception** with five conditions (CONVENTIONS §6 ruling A). Conditions: scope is this widget ONLY · `BindWidgetOptional` members are still declared and a child is constructed **only if still null after `Super::RebuildWidget()`**, so a future WBP wins with zero C++ change · **`/Game/UI/WBP_AssistantConsole` is RESERVED now** · the `USessionMenuWidget` contract (FString/int32/bool/uint8-only BIEs) is unchanged · **verification is a human pixel check.** The fallback costs **one art task and zero C++ change** and may be taken at any time.

The approved plan is internally inconsistent: its GBNF sketch shows `kind` as a *rule* (singular by nature) while its go/no-go bar #5 scores exact-match on `{intent, KINDS, COUNTS, where}` — **plural**. Plural is the intent; the sketch never drew the top-level object. **`FSiegeAssistantCommand` now carries index-aligned `TArray<FName> Kinds` + `TArray<int32> Counts`, hard cap `SiegeAssistantMaxSelectionKinds = 3`**, enforced in **both** the grammar and the parser (an unbounded repetition rule is exactly what a small model rambles into). Parallel arrays, never an array of structs — that is what preserves the `FName`/`int32`-only property and the M8 P2 "takes it as-is" claim (~30 bytes at the cap). **Found while specifying TASK-426's expected outputs, which is precisely what that task is for.**
16. **⚖️ THREE POST-DELIVERY RULINGS ON THE SEALED CORPUS (2026-08-02, after TASK-426 landed).**
    **(a) THE INTENT-IN-`Notes` ENCODING IS ACCEPTED.** The pinned header has no `ExpectIntent` column but bar #5 scores intent, and rows like `charge with the footmen` vs `send the footmen at their castle` differ in nothing else. TASK-426 **correctly refused to add a 10th column after the seal** — that would have silently broken the contract TASK-410's parser is written against — and prefixed every `Notes` cell instead. **The runner extracts it with `^intent=([a-z]+); `**; values are the 7 intents plus `none` (Refuse) and `unasserted`. Accepted because it costs a one-line regex, **zero corpus edit**, and the values predate any prompt, so the seal holds. Written into CONVENTIONS §11 and TASK-410's spec.
    **(b) 🚩 AN EMPTY CELL IS OVERLOADED — v1-ACCEPTED, NON-BLOCKING.** It means *"not asserted"*, so a row whose correct answer is *"this field IS empty"* (`rally`, `fallback`) cannot be positively asserted; it lives in `Notes` prose. ⚠️ **Scored as SKIPPED, never as matched** — reading empty as a pass would manufacture free score on exactly the rows that assert least. A sentinel (`<none>`) is a **new** corpus, never an edit to the sealed one.

17. **⛔ `mage` STAYS UNALIASED, PERMANENTLY (CONVENTIONS §9b — a named prohibition, not a note).** `sorcerer` and `wizard` are different cards and share **no** alias; the sealed corpus carries `the mage` in both files (`DEV-06`, `HOLD-09`) as a **`Clarify`** row. **Aliasing it to either card turns an honest clarification into a confident wrong command** — the exact failure class this architecture exists to prevent. Written as a prohibition because *"add the obvious alias"* is what a well-meaning future task will do, and it would read as an improvement while silently deleting a gate row's meaning. **Automatic QA FAIL, in this batch and every later one.**

    three synonym tables. **This is a DATA task — no C++, no new class, no gameplay change.**
    **(1) `UnitSynonyms`** — one row per commandable CardID, `Canonical` = the lowercase canonical symbol the grammar emits (e.g. `footman`),
    `Aliases` = the natural words a player types. **Read `Docs/Data/cards.csv` for the authoritative CardID list — never invent a unit.**
    Minimum coverage: plurals and colloquials (`footmen`, `infantry`, `soldiers` → `footman`; `bowmen`, `archers` → `archer`; `knights`,
    `cavalry`, `horsemen` mapped to their **actual distinct cards**).
    ⚠️ **THE ONE THAT MATTERS: `sorcerer` AND `wizard` ARE DIFFERENT CARDS AND MUST NOT SHARE AN ALIAS.** The Sorcerer is the non-attacking
    ley-warden empowerer; the Wizard is the AoE fireball caster. A shared alias makes the assistant confidently command the wrong unit, which
    is exactly the valid-shaped-wrong-command failure the whole design exists to prevent. **No alias may appear in two rows** — check it.
    **(2) `PlaceSynonyms` — THE SEVEN CANONICAL SYMBOLS ARE PINNED IN CONVENTIONS §9a AND ARE NOT YOURS TO SPELL:**
    `enemy_castle` (`their castle`, `the enemy base`, `red castle`) · **`own_castle`** (`home`, `our castle`, `base`) · `mid` (`middle`,
    **`the middle`**, `mid lane`) · `ancient_ground_near` (`the nearest ancient ground`, `the near ancient ground`, `our ancient ground`) ·
    `ancient_ground_far` (`the far ancient ground`, `their ancient ground`) · **`nearest_mine`** (`the nearest mine`, `the mine`) · `hero`.
    ⚠️ **It is `own_castle`, NOT `my_castle`** — a `my_castle` spelling was proposed after the corpus sealed and was **overruled**, because
    `HOLD-06` asserts `own_castle` and the holdout is frozen. **V1's place vocabulary is CLOSED** — no free-form map references, no "over
    there". Widening it silently changes Zone A and invalidates the measured accuracy.
    **(3) `IntentSynonyms`** — the 7 canonical intents (`send`, `guard`, `ambush`, `follow`, `charge`, `fallback`, `rally`) with natural
    phrasings. ⚠️ **`charge`/`fallback` are ARMY-WIDE stances with no selection; `send`/`guard`/`ambush` are selection-bearing.** Do not give
    an army-wide verb an alias that reads as selective (e.g. `attack with the footmen` must NOT alias to `charge`) — that mapping is the exact
    friction the executor design exists to avoid.
    **(4) KEEP IT SHORT AND ORDERED.** This table is serialized into **Zone A**, which is under a shared ~350-token budget and **must be
    byte-stable** — so keep aliases tight (aim ≤ 4 per row) and let the ordering be deterministic. A bloated table eats the snapshot budget.
    **(5) ⚠️ DECLARE REACTIVE COVERAGE (CONVENTIONS §11).** By the time you run, `Docs/Data/assistant_eval_*.csv` exist. Covering a phrasing a
    corpus row uses is **legitimate work** — the corpus is a realistic distribution of what players type, and requirements flowing into the
    vocabulary is the right direction. **But list, in the handoff, every alias you added BECAUSE a corpus row needed it**, so the reader knows
    that coverage was reactive rather than independently derived. ⛔ **Never narrow or edit the corpus to match your table** — that is the
    forbidden direction and it voids the go/no-go number.
    **(5a) THE REACTIVE-ALIAS DEBT IS ALREADY KNOWN AND IS A REQUIREMENT, NOT A SUGGESTION** (`handoffs/TASK-426-artist.md` §"Reactive-coverage
    debt", cross-checked by the manager). These aliases are asserted by sealed corpus rows and **must exist**:
    `infantry` → `footman` · `footmen` → `footman` · `bowmen` → `archer` · **`horsemen` → `cavalry` (⚠️ NOT `knight` — they are two different
    cards)** · `the middle` → `mid` · `their castle` / `the enemy base` → `enemy_castle` · `our castle` → `own_castle` ·
    `the nearest ancient ground` / `the near ancient ground` → `ancient_ground_near` · `the far ancient ground` → `ancient_ground_far` ·
    `the nearest mine` → `nearest_mine`.
    **(5c) ⚖️ WARN-6 AND WARN-7 FROM `qa/TASK-419.md` ARE EXPLICIT ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ON THIS TASK — NOT background reading.**
    **⚠️ WARN-7 IS THE ONE THAT WILL OTHERWISE BE MISSED, AND IT IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS TASK IS DANGEROUS.** The two new automation guards
    read `GetDefault<USiegeAssistantVocabulary>()` and `NewObject<USiegeAssistantVocabulary>()` — **both carry the C++ CONSTRUCTOR DEFAULTS.
    NOTHING IN THE SUITE EVER LOADS THE AUTHORED ASSET.** So the guards protect the **fallback** table and **not the shipped one**, and
    **this task is precisely where `militia_mob` or a caster alias could return — into the table that actually ships in Zone A.** The suite
    reads as *"the bug can't come back"*; what it means is *"the bug can't come back in the file we just fixed."* **No test will ever catch a
    defect you author here.**
    **THE TWO RULES, VERIFIED AGAINST THE AUTHORED `.uasset` AND NEVER AGAINST THE CDO:**
    **(a)** no unit `Canonical` contains a separator — it is the **CardID lower-cased, derived from `Docs/Data/cards.csv`, never spelled by

    **(b)** **no alias on any row embeds `mage` / `caster` / `spellcaster` as a SUBSTRING** — substring, not equality, because

    request.

    robustness"; that reintroduces exactly the class this design removes.
    **(4) CANCELLATION VIA `llama_context_params::abort_callback` — the ONLY correct mechanism.** Polling a flag after generation is far too
    late during a long prefill. `CancelActiveRequest()` routes through it.
    **(5) THREE TIMEOUTS:** soft **4 s** (UX only — keeps waiting, just tells the FSM to say something), hard **10 s** (abort), token budget
    **96**. Values are `EditDefaultsOnly`/named constants, **corrected from TASK-413's measurements**, all flagged for Jonathan's feel pass.

    header, `llama.h:735` is the real symbol**) prefix retention keyed on the **Zone A + Zone B** prefix so turn two reuses it
    (**~70 % prefill drop** is the bar).
    **(7) SAFETY:** SEH around the eval · **`bAssistantFaulted` session latch** · **the completion delegate ALWAYS fires on the GAME THREAD** ·
    a GGML crash must not kill the game · shutdown joins the worker cleanly and frees the model.
    **(8) THE PLUGIN STILL KNOWS NOTHING ABOUT SIEGEBOUND.** No `#include` of any game-lane header, no Siegebound type in any signature.
    The entire API surface between the two lanes is `(prompt, gbnf) → string`. **A Siegebound include in this file is a QA FAIL.**
    ⚠️ **AND NO MULTI-TURN LOOP** — this class exposes exactly one single-shot call and holds **no conversation state whatsoever** (§1).
    **(9) 📥 FOLDED IN BY THE MANAGER 2026-08-03 (from `qa/TASK-416.md` — both items were CORRECTLY deferred to you, not neglected):**

    **(1) TWO FILES, PINNED HEADER, IDENTICAL IN BOTH, character-for-character:**

    `Id,Sentence,ExpectOutcome,ExpectKinds,ExpectCounts,ExpectWhere,ExpectTriggerKind,ExpectTriggerAtLeast,Notes`
    `ExpectOutcome` ∈ **`Execute` | `Clarify` | `Refuse`**. `ExpectKinds` / `ExpectCounts` are **`|`-separated and index-aligned**
    (the `FSiegeAssistantCommand` shape — ruling 15; **`Count` 0 means "all"**). An empty cell means that field is **not asserted** for the row.
    **THE TWO FILES MUST BE COMPARABLE IN DIFFICULTY** — do not put all the easy rows in one. Distribute each adversarial category across both.
    **(2) SENTENCES ARE NATURAL PLAYER ENGLISH, NOT CANONICAL SYMBOLS.** Write what a person actually types mid-fight — lowercase, terse,
    unpunctuated, sometimes clumsy. ⚠️ **Do NOT phrase rows to match a synonym table** (`DA_AssistantVocabulary` does not even exist yet, and

    · **ambiguous quantities** ("send a few footmen", "most of the archers", "send 10" with no unit named);
    · **units that do not exist in the live roster** ("send the catapults") ⇒ `Refuse`;
    · ⚠️ **THE SORCERER/WIZARD COLLISION — the single most important rows in the file.** They are **different cards**: the Sorcerer is the
      non-attacking ley-warden empowerer, the Wizard is the AoE fireball caster. Include rows for each **by name**, plus at least one row using
      a word that could plausibly mean either ("send the mage to the ancient ground") ⇒ `Clarify`. A shared alias would make the assistant
      confidently command the wrong unit — **the exact valid-shaped-wrong-command failure this whole design exists to prevent**;
    · **a selection verb mixed with an army-wide one** ("charge with the footmen", "everyone fall back except the miners") — `charge`/`fallback`
      are **latched army-wide stances with no selection**, so these must NOT map to a selective order;
    · **MULTI-KIND selections** (ruling 15) — including the flagship *"send 10 footmen with a sorcerer to the nearest ancient ground"*, a

    · **out-of-scope requests that must be REFUSED, not attempted** ⇒ ⚠️ **the AI never plays cards and never spends gold** (Jonathan's ruling):

    · **plurals/colloquials** (`footmen`/`infantry`/`soldiers`, `bowmen`, `horsemen`) and **`all`** ("send everyone at their castle").

⛔ **No handoff, QA report, board entry or Slack post may frame an early stop as a failure, a cancellation, or *"the fine-tune didn't happen"*.** Fixing D1 is **hours**; QLoRA is **weeks**. ⚖️ **The reason this is dated before the run is that an early stop is only credible as a success if it was declared one in advance** — declared afterwards it reads as consolation, which is how a pipeline learns to push past its own stops. ⚠️ **And the symmetric trap is named too: this is NOT a licence to stop early to avoid hard work.** *"It felt like the wire format was the problem"* is not STOP 1 — **a stop is a number, in writing, against a rule written before the run**, and its denominator is M0's measured noise floor.

## CONSOLE-CLOSE — decomposed 2026-08-03, MID-PLAYTEST, on Jonathan's live directive — TASK-505..508

**Jonathan's directive, verbatim:** *"we need a way to be able to close the AI chat window in the game. Lets make it to where if you press "enter" without anything typed in the box then it will close. After that I will resume testing"*.

**Law was written FIRST (house rule):** CONVENTIONS "In-match LLM command assistant" **`AS-§6` RULING A-2 — THE CONSOLE'S CLOSE ROUTES** (the four routes enumerated, the close-is-not-a-cancel rule restated, the ordering hazard named, and Escape left OPEN as Jonathan's).

### ⚖️ THE FOUR MANAGER RULINGS FOR THIS BATCH

**RULING 1 — THE CHANGE LANDS IN `HandleTextCommitted`, NOT IN `SubmitPressed`. This is the whole design decision and it is one symbol wide.**
`HandleTextCommitted` **already** filters to `ETextCommit::OnEnter` only — it exists because `OnUserMovedFocus` and `OnCleared` arrive at the same delegate and *"treating either as an order would let a click elsewhere submit a half-typed sentence."* ⇒ **That filter is exactly Jonathan's trigger: an `Enter` keypress, and nothing else.** ⛔ **`SubmitPressed` is `BlueprintCallable`, reachable from routes that are not the key, and its empty-string branch is a DIFFERENT, ratified protection (no model call on a blank prompt — queue depth is 1). Moving the close there would make "some other caller passed an empty string" mean "close the window", which nobody asked for.**

**RULING 2 — ⚠️ THE ORDERING QUESTION IS UNMEASURED, SO THE FIX IS BUILT TO BE CORRECT IN *BOTH* WORLDS RATHER THAN TO BET ON ONE.**
⛔ `Enter` would now do **three jobs**: open the console (TASK-445's `IA_AssistantConsole`) · submit a typed line · close it when empty. **World A — Slate consumes the key while the input box has focus** (TASK-445's reasoning, ⚠️ *"reasoning, not measurement"*): Enhanced Input never sees it, the controller toggle never fires while open, the three jobs never collide, and route 4 is the ONLY thing that can close the box. **World B — Enhanced Input sees it too:** an empty-box press would `CloseConsole()` → broadcast → the controller clears the posture → `OnAssistantConsolePressed` then finds the console CLOSED and takes the **open** branch ⇒ **close-then-reopen, which reads to the player as "the close key does nothing."**
⭐ **AND JONATHAN'S OWN REPORT IS EVIDENCE FOR WORLD A, WHICH IS WHY THIS FIX IS THE RIGHT ONE:** the controller's toggle already closes the console (`SiegePlayerController.cpp:4270`, close-first and un-gated). **If Enhanced Input were receiving `Enter` while the box had focus, the console would ALREADY close on `Enter` — and his complaint is that it does not.** ⚖️ **That is corroboration, not a measurement, and it is recorded as corroboration.**
⇒ **TASK-505 ships a re-open suppression window and states which world it relied on.** ✅ **The suppression is SAFE ALREADY: `OnAssistantConsolePressed` re-reads `IsConsoleOpen()` after `OpenConsole()` and releases the posture on a refusal (`:4365`) — so a refused re-open cannot strand the cursor in `GameAndUI`.**

**RULING 3 — ⛔ THE FIX IS COMPILED NOW AND COMMITTED LATER, WITH TASK-481. THE COMPILE AND THE COMMIT ARE SPLIT ON PURPOSE.**
TASK-481 is **PARTIAL**: Stage A compiled clean and its **source is deliberately UNCOMMITTED** because `FT-§16`'s dev-split proof could not run (no editor, no MCP). ⚖️ **I rule the fold IN for the compile and the commit, and OUT for the measurement:**
- ✅ **FOLD THE SOURCE.** The console widget is **not on the dev-split's path** — a different TU, zero call sites from `SpikeEval`, no shared symbol. Adding it cannot move a score that grades JSON emitted by the spike. **One compile, one commit, one gate — Jonathan does not pay for a second cycle.**
- ⛔ **DO NOT FOLD THE MEASUREMENT INTO HIS PLAYTEST.** The §16 proof needs an exclusive editor + PIE + **the whole GPU** (`SC-§16`: two model-load paths WON'T FIT ⇒ one lane per session), and **Jonathan is at the keyboard and wants to play.** ⇒ **TASK-507 is COMPILE-ONLY: no MCP, no PIE, no `SpikeEval`, no Git.** The measurement and the single combined commit stay exactly where they are, in TASK-481, and run when he hands the machine over.
- ⚠️ **THE COST OF THIS RULING, STATED: Stage-A source AND the console fix both sit UNCOMMITTED through his playtest.** That is already the state Stage A is in; the fix adds one more uncommitted file to the same pending commit. **`main` stays 29 ahead and nothing is pushed.**
- ⛔ **IF TASK-505 FAILS TO COMPILE, THE CONSOLE FIX IS THE THING THAT STOPS — NEVER STAGE A.** Build-master reports the errors and hands back to the programmer; **it does not `git checkout`/revert an uncommitted file** (that would destroy work that has no commit to fall back to).

**RULING 4 — 🧑 THE ESCAPE QUESTION GOES TO JONATHAN AS A QUESTION, AND IT DOES NOT BLOCK HIS FIX.**
⚠️ **This is the SECOND time the same underlying need has surfaced** — flagged item (t) recorded that **Escape does not close the console** (TASK-444 left it unabsorbed on purpose so the shipped cancel routes keep firing), and now he has hit the missing close in play. ⇒ **The conventional answer is Escape, and it needs no key overloading at all** — but **§2 says the assistant may never degrade a shipped key**, and Escape already means *"cancel"* in placement, targeting and group-pick. ⛔ **I am not deciding it.** It rides TASK-508 as a one-line question at the playtest he is already doing. **His answer gets written into `AS-§6 A-2`, not into a code comment.**

This also binds the `Z`-accept handler.**
3. **REAL EXCLUSION IN THE SCHEMA** — *"all except X (and Y)"* becomes a genuine executable order, ⛔ **not a clarify-only fix.** He **DECLINED** the count-controlled variant (*"all except 5 archers"*) ⇒ **whole-kind exclusion only, and `AS-§20.1` makes that limit STRUCTURAL (a bare-symbol array has no shape for a count) rather than documentary.**

### ⚖️ THE SIX MANAGER RULINGS FOR THIS BATCH

**RULING 1 — FOUR INDEPENDENT LANES, FIVE IMMEDIATE STARTS, AND THE PARALLELISM IS REAL BECAUSE FILE OWNERSHIP IS EXCLUSIVE — NOT BECAUSE I WANTED FIVE.**
The lanes touch **disjoint file sets**, which is the only thing that makes concurrent authoring safe in a single-UBT-unit module. ⛔ **Every file below has exactly ONE owner at a time; where two tasks need the same file they are SERIALIZED and the second is `blocked-by` the first FOR OWNERSHIP, not for logic.**

| file | exclusive owner(s), in order |
|---|---|
| `SiegeKeyboardLayoutSubsystem.{h,cpp}` | **516** |
| `SiegeAssistantSnapshot.{h,cpp}` | **517** → **521** |
| `SiegeAssistantCommand.{h,cpp}` · `SiegeAssistantGrammar.cpp` | **518** |
| `SiegeAssistantComponent.{h,cpp}` | **520** → **522** |
| `SiegeAssistantConsoleWidget.{h,cpp}` | **519** |
| `Tests/SiegeAssistantSelectionTest.cpp` (NEW) · `Tests/SiegeAssistantZoneATest.cpp` | **523** |
| `Docs/Data/assistant_eval_dev.csv` | **524** |

⇒ ▶ **DISPATCHABLE IMMEDIATELY, IN ONE MESSAGE: TASK-516 ∥ 517 ∥ 518 ∥ 520 ∥ 524.**
⚠️ **TASK-523 (tests) IS DELIBERATELY SERIALIZED BEHIND EVERY IMPLEMENTATION IT TESTS** — the `KBD` RULING-1 reasoning, restated because it is the reason the batch buys a real reviewer: **a test authored beside its subject can only encode the pin, and the pin is what the implementation was written from too. The independent check comes from the test author READING the finished code and DISAGREEING with it.**
✅ **TASK-524 (corpus) IS THE OPPOSITE CASE AND STARTS IMMEDIATELY ON PURPOSE:** corpus rows are **expectations authored from the player's sentence**, and authoring them *after* seeing the implementation is how a corpus quietly becomes a description of the code instead of a test of it (§12b's self-grading shape).

**RULING 2 — ⛔ ZONE A GAINS **RULE LINES ONLY**. NO NEW FEW-SHOT SENTENCES. THE SEAL DECIDES THIS, NOT TASTE.**
The few-shot law requires **literal disjointness from all three corpus files**, and 🔒 **`assistant_eval_holdout2.csv` is SEALED and this batch may not open it.** ⚠️ **TASK-430 already proved a new sentence CANNOT be cleared without opening them** — two agents on the same public brief converged on the same invented noun and **neither could see it**. ⇒ **A new few-shot would cost the seal; a rule line costs nothing** (the disjointness law binds example *sentences*, not instructions). ⭐ **And the ladder wave MEASURED a decision-ordering rule beating an exemplar at this exact seam** (the `who:"none"` collapse was fixed by a rule with a testable antecedent, after emphasis lost 4-to-1 to the prompt's own competing instructions). ⚠️ **I am overruling the MECHANISM the exploration proposed (a `who:"all"` few-shot) while keeping its DIAGNOSIS intact, and I am saying so rather than quietly substituting.** ⛔ **THE COST IS REAL AND GOES ON THE HUMAN GATE: a rule is a weaker teaching signal than an exemplar for an output SHAPE the model has never seen. If TASK-527 shows exclusion or "all units" still missing, the next pass may spend a few-shot — with HIS instruction, and with a mechanical boolean absence certificate, never a read.**

**RULING 3 — ⛔ `all_except` IS LEGAL *ONLY* WHERE `SiegeAssistantIntentTakesSelection()` IS TRUE. THIS IS READ OFF THE EXECUTOR, NOT CHOSEN FOR SAFETY.**
`Charge` and `Fallback` execute by calling **`ASiegePlayerController::ApplyArmyWideStance(...)` — the SAME shipped API the `T` and `E` keys call, release law included** — and `Rally` calls `AHeroCharacter::Rally()`. ⛔ **None of the three passes through the selector**, so an exception could only be honoured by editing a shipped controller API two keys depend on, **or by building an assistant-side "army-wide except" path — which is exactly the *"never a parallel implementation, never a better one"* that `AS-§2` forbids by name.**
⇒ **The parser REFUSES `all_except` on `charge`/`fallback`/`rally` (`ExcludeConflict`).** ⛔⛔ **The alternative — parsing the exception and then dropping it, which is what the shipped comment *"the executor ignores the selection"* would do — turns *"fall back except the miners"* into *"fall back INCLUDING the miners"*: a valid-shaped wrong command that looks obeyed. That is the single failure class this whole design exists to prevent.**
✅ **HIS OWN EXAMPLE IS FULLY SERVED: he wrote *"send all units except for some"* — `send` is selection-bearing.** ⚠️ **`DEV-08` (*"everyone fall back except the miners"*) is the CORPUS AUTHOR's framing, not his; it KEEPS its `Clarify` verdict and gets a REWRITTEN reason** — ⚖️ **a row whose verdict stays the same for a completely different reason is the most misleading state a corpus row can be in.**

**RULING 4 — ⭐ THE ROOT-CAUSE FIX IS THAT `other_kinds:` MUST PRINT **NAMES**, AND HIS CAP RULING SHIPS UNCHANGED BESIDE IT.**
⛔ **Raising the cap to 13 does NOT guarantee 13 rows print.** The roster is **elastic**: `RosterBudget = SnapshotTrimBudgetChars − ZoneBCharReserve − Head − Tail`, and **the `order:` line is IN the Tail**. **At 13 kinds the block measures ~887 against ~893, so roughly SEVEN CHARACTERS of a longer typed sentence re-collapses a kind — and it collapses the Sorcerer, every time, because `Sorcerer` is the LAST `DT_Cards` row.** ⇒ **A player who types a long order gets the original bug back, silently.**
⇒ ⛔ **`other_kinds: sorcerer, cleric (5 units)` — a collapse may hide a kind's NUMBERS; it may never hide its NAME.** ✅ **This closes the class at ANY cap and ANY board size, costs FEWER characters than the row it replaces, and makes Zone A's `[FORCES]` refusal rule TRUE again** — the grammar has always admitted every collapsed kind, so the sampler could name a unit the prompt never showed it.
⚖️ **HIS RULING 1 IS NOT SUBSTITUTED FOR — the cap goes to 13 exactly as he ruled. This is an ADDITIONAL repair he was not offered because it had not been found yet, and the two compose.** ✅ **`t0` is unaffected by the format change: at 13 kinds nothing collapses, so both lanes still print `other_kinds: none`.**

**RULING 5 — ⛔ ONE GATE, ONE COMPILE, ONE COMMIT — AND THE ORDER SATISFIES `SC-§27b` STRUCTURALLY, NOT BY PROMISE.**
**All nine authoring tasks (516–524) land BEFORE TASK-525**, which precedes the single compile+commit at **TASK-526**. ✅ **No second gate is owed.** ⚠️ **The one path that reopens it is a gate FAILURE** — a fix landing after the PASS gets `SC-§27`'s **diff-scoped** verdict (changed lines + the fences the fix must not have disturbed), ⛔ **never a re-litigation of the passed design.** ⚠️ **And if build-master authors a compile fix, that diff is CODE and owes a `SC-§27` diff-scoped verdict before the commit — boarded then, not assumed away.**

**RULING 6 — ⛔ `ZoneBCharReserve` IS BOARDED (TASK-528) AND IS **NOT DISPATCHED** IN THIS BATCH, BECAUSE THE MEASUREMENT IT REQUIRES DOES NOT EXIST YET.**
It is the **highest-leverage lever on the 6-char headroom** — a documented **~124-char over-charge** (measured Zone B readings 68 / 71 against a 192 reserve), and **lowering it can only WIDEN the roster.** ⛔ **But its own header says, in terms, *"set it from the SHIPPED builder's PRINTED worst case"* and *"re-measure it, do not eyeball it"* — and the printed figure still does not exist.** ⇒ **It is boarded with the exact procedure so it is not lost, blocked on a live `zoneB_chars` reading, and ⛔ if the reading does not happen the task does not proceed — it does not fall back to arithmetic.** ⚖️ *A tighter constant taken from a derived figure is the precise defect §12g exists to prevent, and this constant's own history is the argument: the number it would replace was itself eyeballed.*

    **(1) THE SHAPE, AND THE REASON IT IS THIS SHAPE:** `"who": {"all_except": ["miner"]}` — **a third SHAPE for an existing key**, ⛔ **never a fourth top-level key.** ⚠️ **The parser validates an EXACT key set and the prompt law emits every key always, so a new top-level key would rewrite all seven few-shots, every corpus row's expected JSON and the parser's key set AT ONCE.** ⇒ ✅ **A `who` shape is STRICTLY ADDITIVE AT THE WIRE: every JSON that parses today still parses, byte-for-byte.**
    **(2) ⭐ BARE KIND SYMBOLS, ⛔ NEVER `{"kind":…,"n":…}` ITEMS.** **Jonathan DECLINED the count-controlled variant** ⇒ *"all except 5 archers"* must have **no shape in the grammar to be sampled into.** ⚖️ **That is §1's *"grammar guarantees existence"* doing the product's work — a declined feature enforced by a shape cannot be reintroduced by a prompt tweak or a tired author.**
    **(3) STRUCT:** add **`TArray<FName> ExcludeKinds;`** as the **SIXTH** field, after the five shipped ones, in shipped order. ⚠️ **The struct's own class comment says *"five fields"* — update it.** ⛔ **Do NOT reorder, rename or re-type anything existing** (`Kinds`/`Counts` stay PARALLEL ARRAYS — the comment already forbids "tidying" them into a pair struct, and the wire property depends on it).
    **(4) GRAMMAR (`SiegeAssistantGrammar.cpp`):** `who ::= selection | except | "all" | "none"`, with **`except ::= "{" "\"all_except\"" ":" except_list "}"`** and **`except_list` a BOUNDED ALTERNATION of exactly 1, 2 and 3 bare kind strings, generated from `SiegeAssistantMaxExclusionKinds`** — ⛔ **the same construction the `selection` rule uses, and generated from the constant so widening the cap widens the grammar automatically.** ⛔ **Emit the `except` alternative ONLY when `bHasKinds`.** ⚠️ **If `_` is not legal in this emitter's rule names, use `exceptlist` and DECLARE the departure (`SC-§15`) — do not silently pick a third name.**

NONE of them passes through the selector.** ⛔ **Honouring an exception there would mean editing a shipped controller API or building a parallel army-wide path, and `AS-§2` forbids the second by name.** ⛔⛔ **The failure this prevents is the one the whole design exists to prevent: *"fall back except the miners"* executing as *"fall back INCLUDING the miners"* — a valid-shaped wrong command that looks obeyed.** ⭐ **Use `SiegeAssistantIntentTakesSelection()` itself as the gate — reusing the shipped predicate means there is no second list to drift.**
    **(6) `SiegeAssistantValidateSelection` KEEPS ITS NAME** and gains the three invariants (≤ cap · no repeats · empty whenever `Kinds` is non-empty). ⚠️ **M8 P2 takes this struct over the wire from a peer that passed through nobody's grammar — that is why the parser re-checks what the grammar already guarantees.**

## UNIT-PATHING — decomposed 2026-08-04 on Jonathan's feature request — TASK-529..540

**Jonathan's directive, verbatim:** *"ok, we need to fix the pathing of the Units. There are many times when a unit recieves a command, and on the way to it, it gets stuck behind a rock. Lets come up with a way to fix that without it being too costly to compute. It may have to be some sort of path calculator but I'm not sure."*

**Design authority = the approved plan `C:\Users\wesel\.claude\plans\ok-there-are-a-cheerful-mccarthy.md`** — plan mode, **every engine claim verified first-hand against installed UE 5.8 source at `C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\Engine\Source` and against the `Saved/Logs/` sessions**, ExitPlanMode-approved. ⛔ **The plan file wins over any board summary. The architecture is NOT re-litigated.**

**Law was written FIRST (house rule):** CONVENTIONS **"Unit pathing — the stuck-unit watchdog + nav-rebuild concurrency (2026-08-04)"**, namespace **`NAV-§N`** — 13 sub-sections: the three Jonathan rulings · the three cited causes · **the three ruled-out theories** · the anti-mill + no-double-driver law with the rung table · the determinism obligation · the `L_Arena` never-save restatement · the tile-pool hazard · naming law + the pinned log tokens · **the pinned cross-task signature registry** · the diagnose-first discharge + the conditional · the gate · the M8 declaration · the known limitations.

📌 **A FINDING RECORDED AT AUTHORING, BECAUSE IT WILL MISLEAD SOMEBODY: `ok-there-are-a-cheerful-mccarthy.md` IS THE SAME PLAN PATH `KBD-§`'s LAW CITES.** The plan-file slot was **OVERWRITTEN** — the file on disk today is **this** feature's plan; the keyboard-layout plan is **gone**. ⛔ **A reader following `KBD-§1`'s citation lands here.** `KBD`'s law is complete in `KBD-§0..§11` and needs no plan re-read; ⛔ **nobody "reconciles" the two by editing the wrong section.**

### ⭐ THE DIAGNOSIS IN ONE SCREEN — ⛔ IT IS NOT A MISSING PATH CALCULATOR

**Movement is ALREADY real pathfinding** — `MoveToActor`/`MoveToLocation` with `bUsePathfinding=true`, at **four sites only** (`SummonedUnit.cpp:2446` · `:2473` · `:2479` · `:2585`, plus `MinerUnit.cpp:867`/`:932`). ⛔ **Jonathan's *"it may have to be some sort of path calculator but I'm not sure"* is ANSWERED by that line, not obeyed literally.** Two real causes, both cited:

- **⭐ CAUSE 1 — the navmesh rebuilds ONE TILE AT A TIME, ~216 s per match.** `DefaultEngine.ini:294`'s `bDoFullyAsyncNavDataGathering=True` costs a hard serialization: `RecastNavMeshGenerator.cpp:5892-5896` submits **`NumTasksToSubmit = 1`** when gathering is off the game thread. **738 blocking HISM instances dirty essentially the whole 28×13 = 364-column grid; MEASURED 326 tiles / ~216 s / ~1.5 tiles/s** (`handoffs/TASK-366-buildmaster.md:143-152`), corroborated by an independent **178 s** figure (`handoffs/TASK-350-buildmaster.md:19`). **Tiles sort by seed location and `GetSeedLocations` collects PLAYER-PAWN POSITIONS ONLY (`:7047-7059`)** ⇒ **the far field settles LAST**, and a unit ordered across the map walks over tiles still holding the **pre-scatter bake**: the navmesh says open ground, the rock's collider says no.
- **⭐ CAUSE 2 — nothing detects a stuck unit.** `UPathFollowingComponent` already declares **`EPathFollowingResult::Blocked` after <10 uu in 5.0 s** (`PathFollowingComponent.cpp:136-144`) — but **there is NO `OnMoveCompleted` override anywhere in the project and ZERO `EPathFollowingResult` references**, so the verdict is discarded and 0.25 s later `SummonedUnit.cpp:2440` re-issues the **byte-identical** request. **A silent 5-second livelock, with no telemetry** (the `Failed` log at `:2485` is gated on `bGoalChanged`).
- **CAUSE 3 — the traversability guarantee is dishonest AND holds a determinism hole.** `Traversability CONFIRMED` fires at **+5.03 s** against a ~3 %-built navmesh (`BattlefieldScatter.cpp:1953` reads `IsNavigationBeingBuilt` idle ~211 s early), and the cull-retry path (`:2044-2049`) **DELETES INSTANCES** on that timing-dependent answer ⇒ **the shipped instance set is not a pure function of the seed** (`TASKBOARD.md:11044`).

### ⛔ THREE THEORIES RULED OUT — RECORDED SO THEY CANNOT BE RE-PROPOSED (`NAV-§2` carries the full evidence)

| ❌ theory | why it is dead |
|---|---|
| **raise `AgentRadius`** | `walkableRadius = CeilToInt(AgentRadius / CellSize)` (`RecastNavMeshGenerator.cpp:5306`); at `CellSize=32`, `ceil(34/32)=2` voxels = **64 uu real clearance**, already covering every capsule (30/40/45/**60** Ogre). ⭐ **Any value in (32, 64] yields a BYTE-IDENTICAL navmesh.** 65+ **loses** walkable area, inflates the gather box, and fails nav registration (`FNavAgentProperties::IsEquivalent`, `Precision=5.f`). The engine forbids the actor-side route outright (`RecastNavMesh.cpp:4246`). |
| **re-save `L_Arena`'s bake** | The `Serialize … loaded empty` warnings fire at `00.44.33:603`, **inside the `LoadMap: /Game/Maps/L_MainMenu` window** (log `:1747`). **`L_Arena` loads at `:1847` with NO warning.** The stale bake is the **MENU map's**. ⇒ ⛔ **NO `L_Arena` save, NO new Jonathan exception — the spent one (`TASKBOARD.md:9485-9489`, *"do not cite it twice"*) stays spent.** |
| **crowd / RVO avoidance** | `UCrowdFollowingComponent` is a **permanent** per-agent per-frame solve at 60–120 units with **no FPS baseline** to measure it — against Jonathan's own *"without it being too costly to compute."* ⛔ **And `bUseRVOAvoidance` avoids *pawns*, not static geometry: rocks are `ECC_WorldStatic` HISM colliders, invisible to it. It would not move a unit around a rock at any radius.** |

## ACCOUNTS — decomposed 2026-08-16 on Jonathan's feature request — TASK-599..610 (Phase 1; Phases 2–3 are gated one-liners) — ⭐ **PHASE 2 DECOMPOSED 2026-08-23 (TASK-639..652, A1 RULED: SUPABASE — see "⚖️ ACCOUNTS PHASE 2" below in this section)**

**Jonathan's request, verbatim (2026-08-16, direct in Claude Code):** *"I want to add the ability to create an account that saves data. This can be a "login" button in the main menu that leads to a "create account" button and a "log into existing account" button. Eventually I want to make the accounts created saved in the cloud so that way people can log in from any device. These accounts will be able to track different deck builds that the user has created and saved, any setting adjustments, etc. Come up with a plan for how we can save that data in the cloud. If we need to use a website I would prefer to use github pages since I already have a github account with a website using github pages. If there is another method that you think is easier to manage and store this data in the could let me know."*

**Law was written FIRST (house rule):** CONVENTIONS **"⚖️ ACCOUNTS — local-first player accounts · profile-scoped saves · the cloud-backend ruling (2026-08-16)"**, namespace **`ACC-§N`**, 10 sub-sections `ACC-§0..§9` incl. the pinned cross-task signature registry (`ACC-§7`) and the naming table (`ACC-§6`). ⛔ **Every task below cites it; no task restates it.** 📌 **There is no plan file — every binding name and number is inline in `ACC-§`.**

⭐ **THE SHAPE: PHASE 1 IS A LOCAL-FIRST ACCOUNT SHELL, BACKEND-AGNOSTIC, FULLY DECOMPOSED AND DISPATCHABLE NOW.** The main-menu **Login** button → the account panel with **Create Account** / **Log into existing account** (his exact two buttons) · a C++ profile model · per-profile decks + settings layered on the EXISTING `USiegeDeckSaveGame` / `USiegeSettingsSubsystem` systems by **slot-name scoping through one seam** (`ACC-§4`) — ⛔ **no rewrite of either save system.** Works fully offline; Phase 2's cloud sync bolts on with zero UI rework. **Phases 2–3 are GATED ONE-LINERS, no IDs, pending Jonathan's backend ruling (A1 — default Supabase; GitHub Pages is RULED OUT as the data store with the mechanism on the record, `ACC-§0`).**

### ⚖️ THE EIGHT MANAGER RULINGS FOR THIS BATCH

**RULING 1 — ⛔ GITHUB PAGES IS NOT A DATA STORE, AND THE RULING CARRIES ITS MECHANISM.** Static hosting; a write path requires a GitHub API token inside the game binary, extractable by any player, granting read/write over EVERY account. `ACC-§0`. It may host a companion SITE later. **Phase 2's default backend is Supabase** (hosted Postgres + email/password auth + RLS + plain HTTPS/JSON that `FHttpModule`+`Json` speak natively; the Supabase connector is already wired in Jonathan's Claude environment). ⚠️ **FLAGGED A1 — his ruling, owed before Phase 2 decomposes. NOTHING in Phase 1 depends on it.**

**RULING 2 — ⛔ GUEST IS THE DEFAULT AND LOGIN GATES NOTHING.** The accountless game stays byte-identical: guest slots `"SiegeDecks"`/`"SiegeSettings"` untouched, every menu flow unchanged (`ACC-§1`). **Login surface = main menu ONLY in P1** — no mid-match identity change (slot swap mid-session + unanswered M8 questions).

**RULING 3 — ⛔ THE HONEST-CREDENTIAL LAW.** P1 credentials are a **local convenience, NOT security** — salted `FSHA1` hex, plaintext never persisted and never logged, and ⛔ **no task/handoff/QA text may call it "secure"** (`ACC-§2`). Real auth is the Phase-2 backend's job (server-side bcrypt via Supabase GoTrue). ✅ **QA criterion: grep the diff for any write/log of the password parameter — ZERO.**

**RULING 4 — ⭐ PROFILE SCOPING IS SLOT-NAME SCOPING THROUGH ONE SEAM.** `USiegeAccountSubsystem::GetDeckSlotName()/GetSettingsSlotName()`; unresolvable subsystem ⇒ guest constant (fail-safe = today's behavior). **The call-site set is ENUMERATED, manager-verified first-hand, not assumed:** five deck sites in two files + the settings lane's single `ResolveSlotName()` choke point — file:line in `ACC-§4`. ⛔ **A bare slot literal outside the two guest-constant definition sites and the tests is a QA FAIL.** The shipped `SiegeSettingsTest.cpp:120` constant assertion survives untouched.

**RULING 5 — 🔨 THE ACCOUNT PANEL IS A CODE-AUTHORED TREE — A NEW, NARROW EXCEPTION ARGUED ON ITS OWN FACTS** (the settings ruling is scoped to `USettingsMenuWidget` only and may not be cited). Five cloned conditions incl. the CORRECTED RebuildWidget order (build tree → set `RootWidget` → `return Super::RebuildWidget();`) and the reserved `/Game/UI/WBP_AccountMenu` (✅ verified absent). `BackdropBorder` HIT-TEST VISIBLE (the click-through-into-Quit lesson). **Rendering correctness closes on Jonathan's pixels (TASK-609), never readback** (`ACC-§5`).

**RULING 6 — ⛔ THE MENU SPLICE WAITS FOR THE COMPILE, AND THE REASON IS `SC-§26`.** The `Btn_Login` graph must reference class `UAccountMenuWidget` — a NEW reflected type. **Live Coding cannot introduce new reflected types; a full editor restart on the new binary is mandatory** ⇒ TASK-607 is blocked-by TASK-606 (the compile gate + editor bounce), never dispatched before it.

**RULING 7 — ⛔ QUIET-MODULE vs THE LIVE FLOOR-REPAIR LANE (the batch's serialization law).** The WAR-ROOM Wave-10 chain (TASK-597 diagnosis RUNNING at decomposition → TASK-598 live traces → a gated repair that will own a compile) runs in parallel. **Phase-1 C++ COEXISTS AS EDITS** (file-collision check: ✅ disjoint — this batch touches no castle/mesh/manifest/`ACastle` file), **but ⛔ NO ACCOUNTS COMPILE GATE MAY RUN WHILE THE FLOOR-REPAIR LANE'S GATE RUNS.** The orchestrator sequences TASK-606/608 against the repair's gate — one gate at a time, whoever is ready first. ⛔ **And in ANY PIE this batch runs: no console sentence typed, no `M` pressed** — the TASK-571 latch and TASK-579's empty-map instrument stay intact (F1's answered flag changed the ORDER, not the protection).

### ⚖️ THE FOUR RULINGS FOR THIS WAVE (full reasoning in `WM-§1..§6` — cited, not restated)

1. **ELEVATION = RUNTIME ONE-TIME TRACE BAKE PER MATCH (`WM-§2`).** Hills re-roll per match seed (verified at source) ⇒ an offline bake lies and a ground-only bake is uniform gray. 7,800 traces once per match, lazy on first open, clamp-normalized so castles don't erase hills. ⛔ No offline asset, no per-frame cost.
2. **POI ICONS ARE DISPLAY-ONLY; `WR-§6`'s CLICK→SYMBOL LAW IS UNTOUCHED (`WM-§1`).** Positions from world actors (`AGoldNode` · `AAncientGround` · `ACastle` — the ally-dot precedent), ⛔ never from a new symbol, grid or coordinate. ⚖️ **D8 stays OPEN — icons ≠ nameable AI places; his ask adds VISUALS, not vocabulary.** `ADeepMine` is NOT a POI (default, flagged).
3. **BLUE DOTS = THE SHIPPED ALLY-DOT LAYER, VERIFIED + MADE LEGIBLE, NOT RE-AUTHORED (`WM-§3`).** Enemy dots stay behind the 30-gold reveal (`WR-§7` stands; own units only, per his words).
4. **TASK-580 (the real snapshot seed) IS UN-HELD — FINALIZED 2026-08-29 on VID-003 (`WM-§5` dated block):** the pristine first-open was NOT cleanly captured (mid-session clip; only with-snapshot strings observed) ⇒ TASK-579's instrument is **RETIRED-AS-MOOT, not observed-passed** — this wave makes markers-on-open the new normal, so the pair is unrepeatable, and Jonathan's verbatim directive supersedes the interim measure. 580 folds into this wave under its own ID. ⛔⛔ **BUT the clip shows markers=0 WITH the with-snapshot branch live (`WarMapWidget.cpp:871-873`'s documented case) ⇒ 580 is `blocked-by` TASK-691 (diagnose-first) — a seed aimed before that ruling might land an equally marker-less snapshot and fix nothing.** ⛔ **The 571 CONSOLE half (TASK-552's sentences + numbers) stays owed separately and is NOT discharged by anything here.**

## MARKS + RECALL + GHOST — decomposed 2026-09-01 on Jonathan's three-part directive — TASK-744..755

**Jonathan's directive, verbatim (three features, one message):** *"With the map that you pull up when walking up to the commander, I want you to be able to click on anywhere on the map, to create a circle on the map at that location. you can hover the mouse over it and use the mouse wheel scroll to make that circle larger or smaller. You can right click to delete that circle. Every time you make a new circle, it gets its own number in the middle of it. The first circle you create is circle "1", the next number you create is circle "2". The next number you create is circle "3", etc. This number system will also us to then communicate with the AI about where exactly we want units to be. For example, I can make 3 different circles and then tell the commander something like "move all units to hold 1" or "move all units to ambush 2", and the AI can use that indicated circle on the map to carry out the command. Also, I want to add a recall feature. From anywhere on the map, you can press "b", and that will allow the player to starting a recall animation similar to league of legends where after 10 seconds they teleport back to their castle and they completely refill their health. During this recall animation the player cannot attack and if they get hit with an attack it interupts the channel and they would have to press "b" again to start it from the beginning. I also want to add a respawn timer. If the player dies at any point during the match, they are dead for 3 minutes. During this time they instead get a ghost creature that they can control that is similar to their original body where it can command units, access the AI commander, and look at the map, it just cannot attack or be attacked. The enemy should be able to see this ghost as well. When the 3 minutes are up they respawn back at the castle."*

**Law was written FIRST (house rule)** — three NEW namespaces in CONVENTIONS.md. ⛔ **Every task below CITES them and ⛔ no task restates them:**
- **`MARK-§0..§6`** — the map marks. `§0` **`D8` CLOSED** · ⭐⭐ **`§1` the ZERO-character Zone-A proof (five source readings)** · ⚠️ **`§2` the Zone-C cost that is NOT zero** · `§3` the six rulings **M-1..M-6** · `§4` the mouse-wheel amendment · `§5` names · `§6` M8.
- **`RECALL-§1..§6`** — the channel. ⭐ `§1` the teleport+heal already ships (and the `ResetHero` trap) · `§2` the `B` binding law · ⛔ `§3` `Escape` untouchable · `§4` the five rulings **R-1..R-5** · `§5` the HELP obligation · `§6` M8.
- **`GHOST-§0..§6`** — death + the ghost. ⭐⭐ **`§0` THE 36× FLAG + the corrected raze record** · ⭐⭐ **`§1` the no-`ITeamAgent` ruling** · `§2` what already ships · `§3` the eight rulings **G-1..G-8** · ⛔ `§4` the possession/cursor law · `§5` names · `§6` M8.
- **AMENDED:** the "Group orders — 3-zone HOLD + AMBUSH" **wheel law** gains a second named consumer (`MARK-§4`) — ⛔ **with ⛔ zero code collision**, because the map's wheel is a Slate widget event and the controller's poll is untouched.

### ⚖️ THE SEVEN MANAGER RULINGS FOR THIS BATCH

**RULING 1 — ⛔⛔ THE THREE FEATURES ARE ⛔ NOT THE SAME SIZE, AND THE BOARD SAYS SO OUT LOUD.**
**Feature 1 (map marks) = 3 tasks and it is the ⭐⭐ BIG ONE — ⛔ not because of the UI, but because a mark is a NEW REFERENT CLASS IN THE AI COMMAND GRAMMAR.** **Feature 2 (recall) = 2 tasks (one of them an art/asset carve).** **Feature 3 (respawn + ghost) = 2 tasks + 1 measurement — ⭐ and it is far SMALLER than it reads, because `SiegeGameMode` already ships the whole teleport-repossess-full-heal respawn and his 3 minutes is ONE NUMBER.** ⚖️ **Sizing them equally would have gold-plated the ghost and starved the referent.**

## LADDER-REDESIGN — decomposed 2026-09-01 on Jonathan's ascent directive — TASK-733/734 (re-scoped) + TASK-737..743

**Jonathan's directive, verbatim:** *"ok, I like what you did with the tower, but I was thinking instead of making it a ramp that you walk up it instead has a ladder you climb up"*

**His second directive, same day, verbatim:** *"they should be attackable while climbing, but they can't attack back."*

> ### ⭐⭐ **READ THE FIRST FIVE WORDS: *"I LIKE WHAT YOU DID."* ⛔ THIS IS ⛔ NOT A REJECTION OF THE TOWER.**
> **The feature, the card, the 30-gold cost, `HIGH-§`, the ×3, the platform concept and the 1,200 uu rise are ⛔ UNTOUCHED. This batch changes exactly one thing: HOW a unit gets to the top.** ⛔ **A task that re-opens any of them is a QA blocker on sight (`TOWER-§8.0`).**

**Law was written FIRST (house rule)** — ⛔ **every task below CITES it and ⛔ no task restates it:**
- **`TOWER-§8`** — the redesign: `§8.0` the scope fence · ⭐ **`§8.1` the FIVE MEASUREMENTS** (M-1..M-5, read at the engine source + our own tree) · `§8.2` what this obsoletes, stated out loud · ⭐ **`§8.3` the PINNED GEOMETRY both lanes build to** · **`§8.4` the pinned sockets + the pinned API signature** · `§8.5` the traversal ruling + its named regression risk · `§8.6` the team gate moves · `§8.7` `BothWays` derived.
- **`TOWER-§9`** — ⛔ **Jonathan's DECIDED climb-vulnerability requirement** (⛔ not a default) + ⭐ **the measured exposure table.**
- **`TOWER-§10`** — the five behaviour rulings **L-1..L-5** (proceeding defaults, ⛔ none blocking).
- **`TOWER-§2a` RE-SCOPED, ⛔ NOT STRUCK** — the 30°/2,078 uu rows are moot for this mesh; the **32.005° ceiling** and every other measurement **bind every future ramp, hill and slope** and size this batch's own deck.
- **`TOWER-§7` AMENDED** — footprint ~2,700 → ~750 uu ⇒ **TASK-735 gets easier, ⛔ not obsolete**, and needs ⛔ **zero spec edits** because it takes the footprint from the mesh.
- **New naming clause: "Static-mesh SOCKET names"** — `<Purpose>` PascalCase; pinned: **`LadderFoot`** · **`LadderTop`**.

### ⚖️ THE FIVE MANAGER RULINGS FOR THIS BATCH

**RULING 1 — ⛔⛔ THE VERDICT THAT SIZES EVERYTHING, AND IT WAS MEASURED, ⛔ NOT RELAYED.** A ladder is ⛔ **not** a geometry swap. **(a)** Recast cannot generate on a 76° face (the ceiling is 32.005°) ⇒ **a nav link is REQUIRED or the deck is an unreachable island**; **(b)** `ConstrainInputAcceleration` **deletes the vertical component of steering input for any walking or falling pawn, every frame, by design** (`CharacterMovementComponent.cpp:8121-8131`) ⇒ **custom movement is REQUIRED**; and **(c)** this project has **zero** nav links, **zero** `MOVE_Custom`, and exactly **one** `SetMovementMode` call in its entire source. ⇒ **This is greenfield traversal work.** Full table + line cites: **`TOWER-§8.1`**.

**RULING 2 — ⭐⭐ THE RIG IS NOW REQUIRED, AND THE MANAGER SAYS SO PLAINLY BECAUSE THE MANAGER IS WHO TOLD HIM OTHERWISE.** `TOWER-§1` deferred the climb clip on the honest ground that **a unit walking up a ramp looks fine unanimated**. **A ladder inverts that** — a unit gliding up a ladder bolt upright reads as broken. ⇒ **TASK-733 moves from *"polish, gated behind his sitting"* to **REQUIRED** and is **dispatchable NOW**; TASK-734 grows from *"drive them onto a walkable surface"* into real traversal work.** ✅ **The good news is unchanged and is repeated rather than buried: it is still ONE clip** — all three ranged units bind `SK_Footman_Skeleton` + `ABP_Footman`, and `RTG_MeshyBiped_to_SiegeBiped` ships.

**RULING 3 — ⭐ THE BATCH IS SEQUENCED SO THE TOWER IS ⛔ NEVER UNASCENDABLE ON `main`.** The re-authored mesh **deletes the ramp**; the traversal code **replaces it**. ⇒ ⛔ **They may NOT land in separate commits.** **ONE QA gate (TASK-741) · ONE compile + assemble + commit (TASK-742) lands the mesh, the clip, the ABP and both code diffs TOGETHER.** `main` goes *ramp-tower-playable* → *ladder-tower-playable* in a single step, with ⛔ **no intermediate state in which nobody can ascend.**

**RULING 4 — ⭐⭐ THE TWO LANES ARE GENUINELY PARALLEL, AND THE MECHANISM IS THE PINNED GEOMETRY + THE SOCKETS, ⛔ NOT OPTIMISM.** The obvious reading is that the code must wait for the mesh (it needs the ladder's coordinates). **It does not: `TOWER-§8.3` pins every coordinate as a BUILD TARGET for BOTH lanes** — the same move that pinned 2,078 uu before any mesh existed — **and `TOWER-§8.4`'s sockets let the code read the real geometry at runtime and fall back to the pinned literals with one warning.** ⇒ **the code is correct before the mesh lands and self-corrects when it does.** ⛔ **Neither lane blocks the other.**

**RULING 5 — ⛔ FILE OWNERSHIP IS DISJOINT AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE TWO *CODE* TASKS PARALLEL TOO.** **TASK-738 is the SOLE owner of `SummonedUnit.{h,cpp}`; TASK-734 is the SOLE owner of `ClimbableTower.{h,cpp}`.** ⚠️ **734 calls an API 738 declares, so 734 does not compile until 738 lands — ⭐ that is the DESIGNED state and it is a shipped precedent** (`MinerUnit.h:330-334`: *"Until that lands, these two overrides do not compile (C3668) — the designed state for this batch, which compiles as ONE UBT module"*). **The signature is pinned in `TOWER-§8.4` and ⛔ neither task may change it unilaterally.**

## HIGH-GROUND + WATCHTOWER — decomposed 2026-08-30 on Jonathan's four-ask directive — TASK-721..734

**Jonathan's directive, verbatim:** *"notice with the map that the entire thing is black and turns to white with higher elevation locations, lets instead make it to where the entire map is green and goes from darker green to lighter green as elevation increases, try to make the green match as closely to the grass as possible. After that, lets give all archers and wizards and range units increased range. Triple the range of their attacks and make their attacks deal more damage the higher elevation they are. I would say that for every 5 feet that their elevation increases, their damage multiplier increases by 10%. Also, lets add a climable tower as a building card, make the cost 30 gold, and any ranged unit can climb it, so you will have to rig a climbing animation for all the ranged units."*

**Law was written FIRST (house rule)** — three surfaces in CONVENTIONS.md, ⛔ **every task below CITES them and ⛔ no task restates them:**
- **`WM-§8`** — an **AMENDMENT to the existing `WM-§2`**, ⛔ not a new namespace (a colour change to a shipped feature does not earn one). `§8a` what does not change · `§8b` the measured-grass law · `§8c` the legibility table · `§8d` the display/gameplay firewall.
- **`HIGH-§1..§8`** — NEW namespace. The pinned feet→uu arithmetic · the relative-to-target ruling · the one seam · the enumerated ranged set · the no-cap ruling with computed worst cases · the ×3 consequences.
- **`TOWER-§0..§6`** — NEW namespace. The one-rig measurement · the ship-first law · the ramp arithmetic · the card · the four behaviour rulings · the scope fences.

### ⚖️ THE SIX MANAGER RULINGS FOR THIS BATCH

**RULING 1 — ⛔⛔ THE FOUR ASKS ARE ⛔ NOT THE SAME SIZE, AND THE BOARD SAYS SO OUT LOUD.**
**Ask 1 (green ramp) = 2 tasks, and one of them is a MEASUREMENT.** **Ask 2 (×3 range) = 3 CSV cells inside a shared data task.** **Ask 3 (elevation damage) = 1 code task — and ⭐ it is the ask that delivers the most play value per line, because it works on the hills that are ALREADY in every match.** **Ask 4 (the tower) = 6 tasks + a gated follow-on chain.** ⚖️ **Sizing them equally would have starved the tower and gold-plated the ramp.**

**RULING 2 — ⛔⛔ `Docs/Data/cards.csv` HAS EXACTLY ONE OWNER (TASK-723), AND BOTH DATA ASKS LAND IN IT.**
The ×3 range cells **and** the new `WatchTower` row are the SAME file. ⚠️ **Two tasks editing one unquoted CSV is a write-race and a column-shift waiting to happen.** ⇒ **One task, one diff, one reimport.** ⚠️ **And the reimport of `/Game/Data/DT_Cards` is an EDITOR step ⇒ build-master's at integration (TASK-731), ⛔ never claimed by 723.** A CSV edit without a reimport is a **no-op that looks done.**

**RULING 3 — ⭐ THE TOWER LANE OPENS WITH A DIAGNOSE-FIRST SPIKE (TASK-725), AND THAT SPIKE IS CHEAP ON PURPOSE.**
⚠️ **The whole no-rig ship-first path rests on one unproven claim: that Recast will generate a walkable surface on a runtime-spawned ramp at this arena's coarsened nav settings.** ⛔ **Authoring a tower mesh before that is answered is authoring on a hope.** ✅ **The answer is ARITHMETIC against `Config/DefaultEngine.ini`'s own pinned agent figures (44° / 35 uu / 34 / 144, `CellSize 32` / `CellHeight 20`) plus a source read — minutes, ⛔ not a PIE session.** ⚖️ **The spike's ruling IS the mesh task's specification**, which is why 727 is blocked on it and not on 726.

**RULING 4 — ⭐⭐ THE TOWER'S HEADLINE FINDING IS A MEASUREMENT, AND IT INVERTS THE ASSUMED COST.**
`SK_Archer`, `SK_Longbowman` and `SK_Wizard` **all bind the ONE shared `SK_Footman_Skeleton`** and share `ABP_Footman`; `RTG_MeshyBiped_to_SiegeBiped` already ships. ⇒ ⭐ **"rig a climbing animation for all the ranged units" is ONE clip (`A_SiegeBiped_Climb`), ⛔ not three.** ⚖️ **The rig is the CHEAP half; the ASCENT MECHANIC is the expensive half.** ⛔ **A per-unit climb set is REFUSED as redundant** (three clips, one identical rig, three near-identical silhouettes).

**RULING 5 — ⛔⛔ ASK 1 AND ASK 3 SHARE A WORD AND ⛔ NOTHING ELSE. THE FIREWALL IS A QA CRITERION, ⛔ NOT A NOTE.**
`WM-§`'s bake **clamps at `GroundZ + 1000`** ⇒ **gameplay reading it would silently stop scaling above 1,000 uu — exactly where a tower and a tall hill live.** ⚖️ **`SHIP-§9`'s class verbatim: correct in the ordinary case, lying in precisely the case the feature exists for.** ⇒ ⛔ **`HIGH-§` reads `GetActorLocation().Z` and nothing else; a `WarMapWidget.h` include on a gameplay path is a BLOCKER on sight** (`WM-§8d`, `HIGH-§3`).

**RULING 6 — ⛔ ONE QA GATE (730), ONE COMPILE + ONE COMMIT (731), THEN HE PLAYS IT.**
His shape, as ever. ⛔ **QUIET-MODULE: the orchestrator confirms no other compile gate is live at 731's dispatch.** ⚠️ **TASK-716/700 (the packaged-zip arena adjudication) is ⛔ NOT this batch's business and this batch must not touch `Tools/Packaging/`.** ⚠️ **If build-master authors a compile fix, that diff is CODE and owes its own `SC-§27` diff-scoped verdict.**

> ⛔⛔ **WHY THEY EXIST, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT WAS MY MISTAKE: ⛔ LANES W AND F WERE BOARDED WITH ⛔ ZERO `qa-reviewer` ROWS.** ⛔ Lane W ran `827`→`834` straight into `TASK-835` (⛔ build-master) and Lane F ran `836`→`842` straight into `TASK-843`. ⇒ ⛔ **as boarded, ⛔ TWO integration tasks would each have committed a ⛔ pile of new C++ that ⛔ NO REVIEWER EVER READ** — ⛔ a ⛔ direct breach of CLAUDE.md's hard gate (*"Nothing is committed to Git without a PASS QA report"*). ⭐ **Lane A had `TASK-810`/`822`; ⛔ W and F had ⛔ nothing equivalent.** ⛔ **The immediate cost was real: `TASK-827` and `TASK-837` reached `ready-for-qa` and had ⛔ NOWHERE TO GO.**

    · **a missing slot yields defaults and does not crash** · **the delegate fires on a real change and does NOT fire on a same-value write.**

    **M8 DECLARATION DUTY: state verbatim in the handoff — "adds no replicated property, no new replicated class, no new relevancy tier."**

    **(1) THE EXECUTOR AND THE SELECTOR — AND THE ONE RULE THAT GOVERNS THEM: CALL THE SAME PUBLIC APIs THE KEYS CALL.** Route group creation
    through TASK-440's `CreateUnitGroup`. ⛔ **Never a parallel implementation, never a "better" one** (§2). Every keyboard command must still
    work byte-identically with the console closed — that is Jonathan's own playtest criterion.
    **(2) ⛔ THE GUARD RUNS BEFORE EXECUTION, ALWAYS, AND INDEPENDENTLY OF THE MODEL.** Call TASK-441's `ValidateCommandAgainstSnapshot`
    against the **live** snapshot and route a rejection to the **existing unsupported-ask outcome**. ⚠️ **A multi-kind selection with one bad
    kind is rejected AS A WHOLE — never silently dropped.** ⛔ **This does not make `DEV-04` pass the eval and may not be reported as accuracy
    progress.**
    **(3) THE CONFIRM STEP — `AwaitConfirm`, AND IT IS A HARD ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, NOT POLISH (§1).** Show (i) a **game-authored** one-line
    summary of the parsed order from the reason-code template table — ⛔ **never a model-produced string** — and (ii) **the ghost circles on the
    ground** via `SpawnGroupCircleDecal`. **Accept executes. Cancel discards, returns to `Idle`, and leaves NOTHING partially executed.**
    ⚖️ **Constrained decoding guarantees SYNTAX, never SEMANTICS — it cannot prevent a valid-shaped wrong command, and the preview is what
    guarantees the rest.** ⚠️ **Ruling 2's table is the measured evidence for this: 4 of 5 stable failures are wrong-place / wrong-count.**
    **(4) THE TOGGLE — READ IT LIVE FROM `USiegeSettingsSubsystem::IsAssistantConfirmEnabled()` AT CONFIRM TIME** (in-memory getter; the
    subsystem is on the GameInstance so it survives the menu → arena travel). **OFF ⇒ skip `AwaitConfirm` and execute.**
    ⛔ **THE LAW THAT MAKES THE TOGGLE SAFE, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT SENTENCE IN THIS SPEC: THE TOGGLE REMOVES A HUMAN REVIEW STEP AND
    NEVER A MACHINE CHECK.** OFF does **not** skip the parse, the `Kinds.Num() == Counts.Num()` invariant, the shortfall/clarification path,
    eligibility, the authority refusal, or the guard in (2). ⚠️ **The tell: every check that runs with the toggle ON runs with it OFF.**
    ⚠️ **Subsystem unresolvable ⇒ behave as if confirm is ON.** **Failing safe means MORE review, never less.**
    **(5) THE DEFERRED INTENT:** latched, kind+count trigger, **120 s TTL**, **1 Hz timer armed ONLY while latched**, **re-resolves on fire and
    returns to `AwaitConfirm`** — ⛔ **it NEVER executes blind**, and ⚠️ **that is true with the confirm toggle OFF as well**: a deferred order
    fires on a board the player has not looked at since they typed it, which is the one case where the review is worth more, not less.
    **(6) MODEL CALL:** exactly one `USiegeLlamaSubsystem::RequestCompletion` per turn, **queue depth 1** (a second request returns false —
    that is the design, not a bug), completion **always on the game thread**. ⛔ **No multi-turn loop, no conversation state, no feeding output
    back in** (§1).
    ⛔ **No controller edits, no snapshot edits, no grammar edits, no `Content/`, no Git, no compile.**
    **M8 DECLARATION DUTY: state verbatim in the handoff — "adds no replicated property, no new replicated class, no new relevancy tier."**
    ⚠️ **AND SAY WHY: the settings value is client-local and governs a LOCAL review step, never an authoritative outcome.**

    (4) by reading rather than by trusting. Post in ⚙️ Dev & QA.

    **(i-2) TASK-437 and TASK-444 BOTH BUILD THE TREE *BEFORE* `Super::RebuildWidget()`**, against CONVENTIONS' then-wording. ✅ **Both are right
    and the LAW was wrong** (`UserWidget.cpp:1214`); it is corrected. ⛔ **Do not file either as a deviation.**
    **(i-3) `AttachConsoleWidget` IS CALLED *BEFORE* `OpenConsole()`, AGAINST MY SPEC'S *"immediately after a successful create/open"* — AND
    THE DEPARTURE IS CORRECT.** TASK-453 settled it by **reading the widget source**: `OpenConsole()` **ENDS** with
    `OnConsoleOpenChanged.Broadcast(true)`, and the component subscribes to that delegate **INSIDE `AttachConsoleWidget`.** ⇒ ⛔ **Attaching
    afterwards would miss the ONLY "opened" broadcast of the first press — the FSM would sit in `Idle` while the player types into a box it does
    not know is open, recovering only on the SECOND open, with no error, no log and no crash.** ⚠️ **That is the `BeginPlay` trap one level

    screen…" §15). ⛔ **The common property that makes these ratifiable rather than licence is that EACH CITES A MECHANISM QA CAN CHECK WITHOUT

## M7.7 tasks (decomposed 2026-07-23) — Deck-builder card details: click a card → "how it works" (TASK-268..272)

**Directive (verbatim, Jonathan, 2026-07-23):** *"lets change the deck builder interface a bit. Make it to where when you click on the display for a card it displays a detailed description on how the card works."*

**Manager rulings (binding for all five tasks; naming law in CONVENTIONS "Deck-builder card details — click-a-card 'how it works' (2026-07-23)", added FIRST):**

1. **Description SOURCE = GENERATED from DT_Cards (option b), not an authored CSV column (option a), not a hybrid (c).** Jonathan asked how the card *works* — mechanics, not flavor — and a **balance pass is explicitly pending** in the Standing backlog. Authored prose would go stale the day the numbers move, and it already HAS: the `Notes` column's `Lightning` row reads *"200 damage to the 3 highest-current-HP enemies in 400"* while that row's live `AoERadius` is **700**. Generated text re-derives from the row every frame, so a balance edit to cards.csv updates all 28 descriptions for free. Consequences: **no `Description` column, no `FCardRow` change, no DT_Cards reimport, and `Notes` is NEVER shown to the player** (it carries GDD refs + implementation identifiers). The only authored copy is a fixed keyword/type GLOSSARY in `DeckBuilderWidget.cpp` — ~15 strings covering keywords, not 28 cards — and mechanic magnitudes that are UPROPERTY defaults rather than CSV columns live there as named constants under the CONVENTIONS glossary-mirror rule.
2. **Add/remove does NOT move — there is no interaction conflict to resolve.** The orchestrator's finding assumed a whole-tile click adds a copy; the shipped tile does not have one. `WBP_DeckCardTile` binds `AddBtn`/`RemoveBtn` only (TASK-118 §element inventory), and TASK-125 made the card art `SelfHitTestInvisible` *specifically* so it never eats those clicks. So the card face is an UNBOUND gesture and details-on-click is purely ADDITIVE: `+`/`−`, the cap-grey, the x/50 counter, the average-cost guide and the exactly-50 `PlayBtn` gate are all untouched. (The new `Btn_CardFace` goes BOTTOM-most in the tile Overlay so the `+`/`−` plate keeps hit-test priority — this is the one thing that could regress M6, and it is an explicit acceptance item.)
3. **View form = NON-MODAL SIDE PANEL, inline in `WBP_DeckBuilder`.** Rejected: a modal (forces open/close per card, blocks `+`/`−`, and 28 cards means a lot of dismissing) and an expanded tile (re-flows the WrapBox and fights the runtime-constructed tree). A persistent right-hand panel lets Jonathan click card after card and compare while still editing the deck. **No new WidgetBlueprint asset** — and per the hard-won lesson, no new widget may ever be made by duplicate+REPARENT (silent RUNTIME-repaint corruption, ~9 wasted fixes); building inline sidesteps the class of defect entirely.
4. **LANE = branch `m7.6-arena10x`; INTEGRATION HELD until Jonathan's W1 look (TASK-219).** The feature's files (`DeckBuilderWidget.{h,cpp}`, `WBP_DeckBuilder`, `WBP_DeckCardTile`) have **zero** overlap with the branch's owned set (L_Arena.umap, DA_BattlefieldScatter, SiegePlayerController, SiegeBotController, CaptureZone), so there is no conflict either way — but the live working tree IS the branch and a checkout to main would swap L_Arena out from under an un-played W1 build. So: develop here, merge to main at the M7.6 Phase-6 gate. The HOLD is the conservative default, not a technical necessity: TASK-268 is file-only (no compile, no Git) and runs NOW; TASK-269..272 touch the editor/compiler/Git and would make the W1 build ≠ the `1e4bd19` build build-master verified — with a small but real risk of leaving `WBP_DeckBuilder` (a match-launch path) mid-surgery when he sits down to play. **FLAGGED: one word from Jonathan ("do it now") lifts the hold — the orchestrator should ask him at the next boundary rather than sit on it, since he is live.** **[CLEARED 2026-07-24: the W1 look is DONE — Jonathan APPROVED the W1 build (TASK-219). The hold is LIFTED; TASK-269 is dispatchable, TASK-270/271/272 follow in chain order (269 compile → 270 panel → 271 tile → 272 commit — order re-confirmed valid). The chain now develops on the live branch HEAD `0295f75`, not the earlier `1e4bd19`.]** **[LANE SHIFT 2026-07-25 — RESUME ON MAIN: M7.6 is now MERGED to main locally (merge `4c680bb`, not pushed); during that merge build-master parked the deck-builder trio UNCOMMITTED on main (milestone entry §7.6). So the chain RESUMES ON MAIN, not the branch — the branch-ownership rationale in this ruling is now MOOT (nothing to swap L_Arena out from under; the diff-guard simply confirms ONLY the three deck-builder files move). TASK-269..272 chain order + the TASK-270-271 completion recipe (handoffs/TASK-270-271.md) + the scaffolding already in the parked WBP are all STILL VALID for the resume. ⚠ COMPILE-VERIFY: TASK-268's `DeckBuilderWidget.{cpp,h}` were STASHED during the M7.6 merge compile, so the feature has NOT been built against M7.5+M7.6 together — TASK-269 must recompile + verify against MERGED main. Both editor-mutating tasks (this chain + TASK-297 SK-LODs) SERIALIZE on one exclusive editor session and run only when Jonathan is not in PIE. Commit backend + WBP together on main at TASK-272, no push.]**
5. **"Detailed description" scope (default chosen, non-blocking):** stat block **AND** keyword/rules explanations — i.e. what it costs, what its numbers are, and what every special rule on it actually does, in plain English with no GDD refs and no class names. **No flavor/lore text** this pass (Jonathan said "how the card works"). Adding a flavor line later = one authored CSV column and a 2-line composer change; it is deliberately not built now.
6. **Verification posture:** the description TEXT is machine-checkable (headless dump of all 28 strings, best-effort; QA reads them against cards.csv by hand). The RENDER and the CLICK are **not** — Slate screen-space UI is uncapturable headless and the deck builder needs a real menu click to open. Those close on Jonathan's eyes (recorded as a WATCH in TASK-272), per the CONVENTIONS pixel/human-check law. No "machine checks pass, ship it."

**FLAGGED for Jonathan (defaults chosen, nothing blocks):** (i) description = mechanics only, no flavor text — say the word for a flavor line; (ii) side panel, not a popup — a modal is a small rework if he prefers it; (iii) the panel is READ-ONLY (no `+`/`−` inside it) so the tile stays the single place a deck changes — a duplicate pair in the panel is easy to add later if he wants it; (iv) the hold in ruling 4; (v) the card TILES are still compact (TASK-125 flag: no fixed card size, sizing lives in the WrapBox slot) — the details panel now carries the big readable card face, which mostly answers that flag, but a proper tile-size pass is still open.

**Manager note (not a task, do not lose):** `CardRow.h`'s `ESpellDelivery` doc comment (lines ~70-76) says the `SpellDelivery` column header is "NOT yet appended to the CSV" — that is **STALE**: `Docs/Data/cards.csv` line 1 now ends with `SpellDelivery` and Fireball/FrostNova carry `HeroLine`. Comment-only correction; deliberately kept OUT of TASK-268's diff to keep QA's surface clean. Fold it into the next task that opens `CardRow.h`.

## W1 Unit-Commands tasks (decomposed 2026-07-23) — Shield Wall stances: ATTACK / HOLD / DEFEND (TASK-273..277)

**Directive (verbatim, Jonathan, 2026-07-23):** *"I want to implement a feature where you can press certain buttons to make the units around you do certain actions, similar to the video game 'shield wall'. For right now, I just want there to be 3 commands: 'hold' which makes all units move towards a specified location and only attack units within that specified location. 'defend' which makes all units head back towards the players castle and only attack units that are attacking the castle. 'attack' which makes all units attack the enemy castle and if there are any buildings or units that are within the spawn of the enemy castle they will prioritize those buildings or units before attacking the castle. This logic would only apply to the units with the 'Standard' targeting profiles... Lets put the 'attack' button on the 't' key, the 'hold' button on the 'r' key, and the 'defend' button on the 'e' key."*

**W1-SCOPED, NOT held.** Develops on `m7.6-arena10x` and INTEGRATES into the W1 build (unlike the M7.7 deck-details chain). Naming law in CONVENTIONS "Unit commands (Shield Wall stances) — ATTACK / HOLD / DEFEND (W1, 2026-07-23)", added FIRST. Applies ONLY to `ECardProfile::Standard` PLAYER (Blue) units; Siege/Support/None bodies + all bot units are UNTOUCHED.

**Manager rulings (binding for all five tasks):**
1. **Command STATE lives on `ASiegePlayerController`** (per-player, player-issued; the T/R/E bindings + ground reticle already live there; M8-ready). Not `ASiegeGameState` (would need per-team arrays; it is flagged local-only-through-M7).
2. **Enemy spawn-box test lives on `ACastle`** (`SpawnBoxHalfExtent` + `IsPointInSpawnBox`) — castle-centered, the unit already holds the enemy-castle pointer via `FindNearestEnemyCastle`. Additive; the bot's TASK-262 `IsPointInBotSpawnBox` is UNDISTURBED. 3-way paired-tunable (player/bot controllers + castle) documented.
3. **`bHasIssuedCommand` latch (default false)** = zero behavior change until the player first presses a key (Q3 default). Latched global stance; future-spawned Standard units adopt it (Q2 default). Play Again resets to Attack + not-issued.
4. **HOLD reuses the spell reticle** ground-target machinery for the location pick (no new reticle system).
5. **HUD indicator is OPTIONAL / fast-follow (Q5)** — gameplay integrates without it; the C++ exposes `OnUnitCommandChanged` so the HUD can bind later.

**E/R/T conflict-check (manager):** the only letter-key gameplay binding today is Rally = **Q** (`HeroCharacter.cpp:182`); cards 1–6, Attack LMB, Jump Space, Sprint Shift, UICursor Left Alt, Cancel RMB/Esc. **E/R/T read as free** — but `IMC_Hero` is a binary `.uasset` the manager cannot text-verify, so TASK-273 MUST confirm in-editor and FLAG any conflict rather than stomp.

**FLAGGED for Jonathan (sane defaults chosen, nothing blocks):** (Q1) HOLD radius default 1500 uu (directive suggested ~1000; raised for the 10× arena) — tune to taste; (Q2) latched global stance, future units inherit — CONFIRM; (Q3) no-command-yet = legacy behavior (ATTACK-without-spawn-priority) until first key — CONFIRM; (Q4) player-only, bot unchanged — CONFIRM; (Q5) HUD indicator + hold-marker in-scope now or fast-follow?; (Q6) DEFEND "attacking the castle" = enemies within `DefendRadius` (2500 uu) of the own castle — the simple/robust default; the alternative (enemies whose target actor IS the castle) is available if he prefers.
